backups.replicateDescription: Sends the backup files to a backup pool of a remote cluster. The copy there is an ordinary backup that can be restored on that cluster. An incremental backup is sent with the earlier backups of its chain that the remote cluster does not have yet, starting from the full backup. Deleting this backup deletes the copy too.

backups.runningDescription: Copies the disks, firmware variables and settings of the VM to a backup pool. The VM keeps running: the disks are copied as they were at one moment, like after a power cut.

backups.deleteDescription: The backup files are removed from the backup pool, and the copies sent to remote clusters are deleted too. This cannot be undone.

backupJobs.fullEveryHint: With 0, every backup is full. With n, backups are incremental where possible and the backup after n incremental ones is full. For example, daily with 6 makes one full and six incremental backups a week.
backupJobs.replicateHint: Each backup the job makes is copied to this backup pool of the remote cluster. Failed copies are tried again at the next run.
backupJobs.deleteDescription: The job stops running. The backups it made are kept.

pools.createDescription: Where volumes are kept: a directory on each node, an NFS export that the nodes mount, an LVM thin pool or ZFS dataset on each node, a Ceph RBD pool, or a volume group shared by the nodes.

kindHint.dir: Create the directory on each node first.
kindHint.nfs: Each node mounts the export under its data directory. Mounting needs Linux nodes running as root. The pool is shared by its nodes.
kindHint.lvm-thin: Create the volume group and thin pool on each node first. Volumes are raw thin volumes kept on the node that creates them, and their snapshots hold disks only. Needs Linux nodes running as root.
kindHint.zfs: Create the dataset on each node first. Volumes are raw zvols kept on the node that creates them, and their snapshots hold disks only. Disks can only revert to their latest snapshot. Needs Linux nodes running as root.
kindHint.rbd: Create the Ceph pool first and put ceph.conf and the keyring on each node. Volumes are raw RBD images that every node of the pool can use, and their snapshots hold disks only. Needs Linux nodes with QEMU's rbd driver (qemu-block-extra) and the rbd command (ceph-common).
kindHint.lvm-shared: Create the shared volume group (vgcreate --shared) on a LUN every node sees first, and run lvmlockd with sanlock or dlm on each node. Volumes are raw logical volumes that every node of the pool can use, without snapshots. Needs Linux nodes running as root.

pools.exportHint: The absolute path the server exports, such as /srv/vm.
pools.optionsHint: Comma-separated options passed to mount -o after nosuid,nodev,noexec,retry=0, such as vers=4.2,hard.

errors.rbdName: Use 1 to 63 letters, digits, _, . or -, not starting with -.
errors.cephUser: Write the Ceph user without the "client." prefix, for example opl instead of client.opl.
errors.rbdConf: Enter an absolute path (starting with /) without control characters, commas, colons or equals signs.
errors.portal: Enter a host name or IP address with an optional :port (1–65535), without spaces, commas or slashes. Put IPv6 addresses in brackets, such as [fd00::5]:3260.
errors.target: Use a target name starting with iqn., eui. or naa., at most 223 characters of lowercase letters, digits, ., : or -.

fence.title: Power-off fencing of {{name}}
fence.description: When the node stops renewing its lease, the leader powers it off with these methods, in order, and recovers its HA VMs without waiting for the watchdog. If every method fails, it waits as before.
fence.none: No methods. The leader waits for the watchdog before recovering.
fence.note: The leader powers nodes off, and neighbour nodes (regular checks), the testing node and the leader read the power, so every node must reach the BMC. IPMI needs ipmitool on every node. Commands get ORBIVISOR_NODE_NAME, ORBIVISOR_NODE_ID and ORBIVISOR_NODE_ADDRESS.

errors.bindDn: Enter a bind DN to use a bind password.
errors.bindPasswordNeeded: Enter a bind password for the bind DN, or clear the bind DN to search anonymously.
errors.bindPasswordAgain: Enter the bind password again: the URL, bind DN or CA certificate changed.
errors.clearNeedsNoBindDn: To clear the saved password, also clear the bind DN.
errors.clearSaved: The bind DN is empty: choose "Clear the saved password" to search anonymously.
errors.timeout: Use a whole number of seconds from 1 to 30.
errors.group: Enter a group DN or remove the row.
errors.issuer: Use https://host[:port][/path] without a query or fragment.
errors.clientSecretAgain: Enter the client secret again: the issuer, client ID or CA certificate changed.

realms.issuerHint: https:// URL exactly as the identity provider reports it, including any trailing slash.
realms.clientSecretHint: Leave empty for a public client (PKCE only).
realms.clientSecretSaved: A secret is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
realms.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. openid is required.
realms.groupsClaimHint: Claim with the user's groups as a list of strings.
realms.redirectUriHint: Register this address with the identity provider. Each node address you sign in through needs its own. Behind a reverse proxy, register the address the proxy passes as the Host.
realms.oidcCaPemHint: Trust only this CA for the identity provider's certificate. Leave empty to use the system roots.
realms.oidcGroupsHint: Group values from the groups claim match without regard to case. A user in several groups gets the highest role.
realms.oidcTestDescription: Checks the identity provider's discovery document and signing keys. No one signs in.

tokens.note: Scripts and tools use API tokens. A token has the role of its owner. orbivisorctl login makes one for the CLI.
tokens.createDescription: The token acts as you, with your role.
tokens.secretDescription: Copy the token now. It cannot be shown again.
tokens.deleteDescription: Anything using the token stops working right away.

cluster.title: Cluster {{name}}
cluster.caNote: Every node's HTTPS certificate is signed by the cluster CA. Import the CA into your browser to stop the certificate warning, and check that its fingerprint matches. Browsers show the SHA-256 fingerprint in uppercase hex, in pairs separated by colons or spaces; compare it with the hex after sha256: (letter case does not matter).
cluster.membersNote: Voters keep the cluster state. A learner is a standby or joining node with the full Raft log. An observer follows a voter outside Raft, so it adds no work to the leader. A witness votes but runs no VMs.
cluster.issueDescription: A new node joins with the token once. Start orbivisord on the new node first.
cluster.issuedDescription: Run this on the new node before {{time}}. It cannot be shown again.
cluster.commandNote: Add --socket if orbivisord on the new node does not use /run/opl/opld.sock.

remotes.pageHint: Other Orbivisor clusters this cluster can see. The status is collected every 30 seconds. What you can do on a remote cluster also depends on the role of the user who owns its API token there.
remotes.addDescription: Register another Orbivisor cluster with its address, the fingerprint of its CA and an API token created on it.
remotes.urlHint: https://host[:port] of a node of the remote cluster.
remotes.confirmFingerprint: This matches the CA fingerprint on the Cluster page of the remote cluster.
remotes.tokenHint: Create it on the API tokens page of the remote cluster. Its user's role there limits what this cluster can do.
remotes.tokenSaved: A token is saved. Leave this empty to keep it.
remotes.deleteDescription: This cluster stops showing it. Nothing changes on the remote cluster, and its API token stays there until you delete it.

errors.probeFirst: Get the CA of this URL first.
errors.confirm: Check the fingerprint against the remote cluster and confirm it.
errors.token: Enter an API token of the remote cluster.
errors.tokenAgain: Enter the API token again: the URL or CA changed.

vmForm.runningNote: The VM is running: its node, disks, and the number, order and MAC addresses of its interfaces cannot change, and if an interface has security groups, only the groups of the interfaces can change. Security groups apply right away; other changes apply from the next start.
vmForm.nicsRunning: Interfaces cannot be added or removed, and their MAC addresses cannot change, while the VM is running.
vmForm.noSecurityGroups: No security groups. Create them on the Security groups page.

errors.name: Use 1–63 lowercase letters, digits and -, not starting or ending with -.
errors.bootOrder: Boot orders must be unique numbers from 1 to 255.
errors.volumeDuplicate: Each disk needs a different volume.
errors.volumeExists: A volume with this name already exists.
errors.macMulticast: A multicast address (odd first byte) cannot be used.
errors.macDuplicate: Each interface needs a different MAC address.

vmForm.scheduleNote: Takes snapshots periodically and keeps only the newest scheduled ones. Snapshots you take yourself are never deleted. All disks must be qcow2, all in LVM-thin pools, all in ZFS pools, or all in Ceph RBD pools.
vmForm.scheduleRaw: {{volume}} is {{format}}, so scheduled snapshots will fail. All disks must be qcow2, all in LVM-thin pools, all in ZFS pools, or all in Ceph RBD pools.
vmForm.scheduleMemoryHint: Memory is saved only while the VM is running and has disks.
vmForm.scheduleMixed: Disks with different snapshot methods (qcow2, LVM-thin pools, ZFS pools, Ceph RBD pools) are mixed, so scheduled snapshots will fail.
vmForm.scheduleSharedLvm: {{volume}} is in a shared LVM pool, so scheduled snapshots will fail.
vmForm.haHint: Runs only on nodes with fencing on. If its node loses the cluster majority, the node stops the VM.
vmForm.haNodeOff: {{node}} has fencing off and cannot run HA VMs.
vmForm.haNoNode: No node has fencing on, so HA VMs cannot run.
vmForm.haRunning: Turn on HA while the VM is stopped.

haStateHint.started: If its node fails, HA starts the VM on another node.
haStateHint.stopped: If its node fails, HA moves the VM to another node but leaves it off.
haStateHint.ignored: HA leaves the VM alone for now: no fencing, recovery or counting. The settings are kept.

vmForm.haGroupHint: Recovers on the group's nodes, higher priority first.
vmForm.maxRestartHint: From 0 to 10 within 10 minutes. After that, HA moves the VM to another node.
vmForm.maxRelocateHint: From 0 to 10 within 10 minutes. After that, HA stops the VM and shows an error; start it again to clear it.
vmForm.haPriorityHint: From 0 to 100. When a node fails, HA restarts VMs with higher priority first.
vmForm.guestWatchHint: Pings the QEMU guest agent (qemu-guest-agent must run in the guest). Once it has answered, no answer for the time below force-restarts the VM. After a guest reboot it waits until the agent answers again. Can be turned on or off only while the VM is stopped.

console.failed: Disconnected. The VM may have stopped or the console is not available.
console.pasteDenied: The browser did not allow reading the clipboard.
console.pasteTruncated: Only the first {{count}} characters were typed.
console.hint: Click the screen to type into the VM. Click outside it to release the keyboard.
console.forbidden: You do not have permission to use the console.

dashboard.mixedVersions: Nodes run different Orbivisor versions ({{versions}}). Finish the upgrade on every node.

subscription.invalid: The subscription key does not match this build.
subscription.over_limit: The cluster has {{used}} nodes, but the subscription covers {{limit}}.

settings.channelHint: Every node gets Orbivisor packages from this channel. Testing gets new versions before stable.
settings.adminOnly: Only administrators can change the settings.

errors.busy: Another settings change is in progress. Try again.

subscription.title: Subscription
subscription.keyHint: Paste the key you received. It starts with opl1.
subscription.removeDescription: The cluster will have no subscription. Nodes on the enterprise channel stop getting updates.

telemetry.title: Telemetry
telemetry.intro: When on, the leader sends a usage report once a day: counts and versions only, without names, addresses or keys.
telemetry.buildDefault: Not set (the build's default endpoint is used if it has one)
telemetry.endpointHint: An https:// address. Leave it empty to use the build default.
telemetry.previewDescription: This is the report the cluster would send now. Nothing else is sent.

shutdown.title: HA VMs on host shutdown

hint.conditional: Freeze on reboot, fail over on power off.
hint.freeze: Turn the node's HA VMs off and start them on the same node when it comes back. HA does not move them meanwhile.
hint.failover: Turn the node's HA VMs off; HA starts them on other nodes after the usual recovery wait.
hint.migrate: Live-migrate the node's VMs away first (node drain, up to 10 minutes), then fail over the remaining HA VMs.

shutdown.note: Applies only when the host reboots or powers off. Stopping or upgrading orbivisord leaves the VMs running.

ha.title: HA capacity
ha.reserveHint: Memory of HA-capable nodes kept free for recovery. Starting an HA VM that would use it is refused. All running VMs count; migrations are not checked.
ha.concurrencyHint: How many HA VMs the leader starts at once on one node during recovery (1–32, default 4).

audit.adminOnly: Only administrators can read the audit log.
audit.refreshFailed: Could not read the audit log again. {{error}}
audit.empty: No audit entries in this range.
audit.unreachable: No audit entries from these nodes (unreachable): {{nodes}}
audit.disabled: The audit log is turned off on these nodes: {{nodes}}
audit.truncated: Showing the newest {{count}} entries. More match; narrow the range or the filters.

haGroups.pageHint: HA VMs in a group are placed and recovered on the group's nodes, higher priority first. When a higher-priority node comes back, a running VM moves back to it by live migration unless the group has No failback.
haGroups.deleteDescription: VMs must not use the group. Placed VMs stay where they are.
haGroups.dialogDescription: HA VMs choose a group in their HA settings. VMs that are already placed are not moved.
haGroups.nodesHint: Priority from 0 to 1000; higher goes first. Empty means 0.
haGroups.restrictedHint: Never place the VMs outside the group. If no group node can take a VM, HA leaves it off and shows why.
haGroups.nofailbackHint: Do not move VMs back when a higher-priority node comes back.

errors.exists: An HA group with this name already exists.
errors.priority: Priorities are whole numbers from 0 to 1000.

haChecks.pageHint: Every node checks these links, ping targets and storage pool paths every 5 seconds and sends the results with its lease. When a check fails on a node for longer than the grace time, the leader reacts as set below. If a check fails on most of the nodes reporting it, the leader treats it as a shared failure and only warns. Only HA VMs are moved.
haChecks.autoNote: Each node also checks its cluster links by itself (cluster-link-1, cluster-link-2 …). Those checks only warn and are shown with the node.
haChecks.graceHint: How long the check must fail before the leader reacts: 10 to 600 seconds (at least two check rounds). Empty means 10.
haChecks.overridesHint: A different target on some nodes, such as another interface name. Other nodes use the target above.

roleHint.management: The node's management network. Failing it only warns unless you choose power-off fencing.
roleHint.storage: The path to shared storage. VMs with disks on it are affected; by default they are restarted on another node, since a VM with stuck disk I/O cannot be live migrated.
roleHint.vm: A network VMs use. VMs with NICs on the bridges behind the interface are affected; by default they are live migrated.

kindHint.link: Passes while the interface has a link. For a bond, losing some ports only shows as degraded; losing all fails.
kindHint.ping: Pings each address once (2 seconds); passes when at least Need addresses answer. Via picks the interface (Linux only).
kindHint.pool: Reads a small file on the pool (NFS, shared directory), checks the iSCSI sessions and multipath paths (shared LVM) or asks the Ceph OSDs (RBD).

haChecks.deleteDescription: Nodes stop running the check. VMs already moved stay where they are.
haChecks.dialogDescription: All nodes in the cluster must run a version that knows HA checks.

errors.exists: An HA check with this name already exists.
errors.reserved: Names starting with cluster-link- are for the nodes' own cluster link checks.
errors.iface: Use an interface name of 1–15 characters without /, : or spaces.
errors.address: Use IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, separated by commas.
errors.need: Need is a whole number from 1 to the number of addresses.
errors.poolRole: Pool checks need the storage role.
errors.action: This role does not allow that reaction.
errors.grace: Grace is a whole number of seconds from 10 to 600.
errors.overrideNode: Choose the node for this override.

placementRules.pageHint: Rules for where VMs run, for all VMs. Hard rules must hold: creating, starting or migrating a VM that would break one is refused. Soft rules are kept when possible. The leader shows broken rules on each VM. VMs already placed are not moved when you add a rule.
placementRules.dialogDescription: Hard rules that contradict each other are refused. Node labels (such as zone=rack-a) can choose nodes.

kinds.soft-node-anti-affinity: Away from these nodes if possible

kindHint.affinity: The VMs always run on one node and move together; one of them alone cannot be migrated.
kindHint.anti-affinity: No two of the VMs run on the same node.
kindHint.soft-affinity: Prefers one node for the VMs; each VM elsewhere adds the weight.
kindHint.soft-anti-affinity: Prefers different nodes; each other VM on the same node adds the weight.
kindHint.node-affinity: The VMs run only on the chosen nodes.
kindHint.node-anti-affinity: The VMs never run on the chosen nodes.
kindHint.soft-node-affinity: Prefers the chosen nodes; another node adds the weight.
kindHint.soft-node-anti-affinity: Avoids the chosen nodes; a chosen node adds the weight.

placementRules.vmNamesHint: Separate names with commas. VMs you create later may be named here.
placementRules.vmTagHint: KEY=VALUE, such as app=web. Every VM with this label.
placementRules.nodeTagHint: KEY=VALUE, such as zone=rack-a. Set node labels on the Nodes page.
placementRules.weightHint: From 1 to 100. Empty means 50. A higher weight matters more.
placementRules.haMayViolate: HA recovery may break this rule
placementRules.haMayViolateHint: If HA can recover a VM only by breaking the rule, it starts the VM anyway and shows the broken rule. Otherwise the VM stays off.

errors.exists: A placement rule with this name already exists.
errors.vmNames: Use valid VM names, each once.
